inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash-flow statement, 'Share-based payments expense (equity-settled)' $43m (SN.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:13451). No separate equity-award tax withholding line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 across the history); awards are satisfied from the Employees' Share Trust / treasury.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow $502m (the 2025 $500m programme). A second $500m programme was announced 2026-05-06: 9,076,588 shares bought for $137m by 27 June 2026 ($116m cash-settled in H1, $113m further obligation booked in equity/other payables), $216m settled by 3 Aug 2026. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (cash out at market = shares in); the FLAT count is funded many times over by buyback cash versus a $43m SBC charge, so flat is the right convention here, not a modelling fiction.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 27 June 2026: ~849m ordinary shares in issue ex-treasury at 17 Feb 2026 (50,961,170 ADS-backed shares = ~6% of shares in issue, FY2025 AR), less 9.08m repurchased in H1 FY2026, plus ~2m released to award beneficiaries, plus ~6m dilutive share-incentive awards (FY2025 dilutive impact 6m, AR note 'Number of shares'). Cross-check: H1 FY2026 diluted EPS 35.2c on $303m attributable = ~861m diluted weighted average, which straddles the half-year buyback. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the remaining ~$384m of the 2026 buyback (post 27 June) is value-neutral and NOT netted against the count or net debt, so count and net debt are on the same 27 June 2026 basis.
inputs.fx_note: Statements, flows and the DCF are in USD; the LSE quote is in pence sterling (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 USD = 100 / 1.3233 = 75.57 GBp, GBPUSD=X 1.3233 (Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-09 21:29 UTC). Parity check against the NYSE ADR (SNN, 1 ADS = 2 ordinary shares, confirmed by EPSA 47.7c/share = 95.4c/ADS in the H1 FY2026 release): 1020.5p x 1.3233 / 100 = $13.50/share x 2 = $27.01 vs SNN $27.24 at 2026-10-09 20:00 UTC, a 0.85% gap -- proves rate, direction and pence basis. The unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are GBp (comparable to current_price); the *_usd twins are the model currency. refresh_price.py moves the price but not the rate; re-derive fx_rate from GBPUSD=X on any refresh.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Net debt EXCLUDING lease liabilities at 27 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 Note 6): borrowings $3,588m (current $508m + corporate bonds $2,670m + private placement notes $410m) less cash and cash equivalents $754m less $12m interest-rate-swap asset = $2,822m. 'cash' is recorded as 766 = 754 + 12 so that total_debt - cash ties to the note's $2,822m. Lease liabilities ($197m: $132m non-current + $65m current) are deliberately EXCLUDED because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B). Net debt including leases was $3,019m; adjusted net debt/EBITDA 1.8x.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: 10-year UST ~4.1% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.9 (diversified medtech, defensive wound-care third) = ~8.6% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (investment-grade bonds/PPs), ~4.0% after tax; weights ~80/20 equity/debt at market (equity ~$11.4bn vs net debt $2.8bn) -> ~7.7%. Rounded UP to 8.0% as the single house rate for all three scenarios. Cyclicality, execution and reimbursement risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and weights, not via per-scenario WACC premiums.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash (capital element $50m in financing + ~$8m lease interest in operating, FY2025) is charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.95% of revenue; lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt; and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: PP&E depreciation $335m + other amortisation/impairment $61m - ROU depreciation $49m = $347m = 5.6% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice through EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; attributable profit = profit for the period. No NCI deduction.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Owner EBITDA, NOT the headline adjusted EBITDA. Company-defined adjusted EBITDA (leverage-covenant basis) was $1,607m = 26.1% of FY2025 revenue; it excludes restructuring, acquisition/integration and legal items that for this serial restructurer recur every year in cash (FY2025: restructuring $83m + acquisition/integration $30m + legal $19m = $132m cash; FY2024 restructuring cash alone $151m). The ebitda_margin_path therefore starts from 26.1% less ~2.1pp of recurring 'non-trading' cash = 23.9% FY2025 actual, and the forward paths net ~1.5pp (fading to ~1.0pp) of such cash out of the adjusted margin. Amortisation of acquisition intangibles ($176m) is non-cash and excluded from both EBITDA and the D&A line; the cash tax path is calibrated to taxes actually paid instead.
inputs.cash_tax_basis: FY2025 cash taxes paid $147m against a modelled FY0 EBIT of ~$1,026m = ~14%; FY2024 $140m (~15%). Guided P&L rate on trading results 19-20%. Cash rate ramps 16% -> 20% over five years as deductible restructuring fades and Pillar Two / UK 25% bite; held at 20% thereafter.
inputs.working_capital_basis: Manufacturer with inventory ($2,113m) + receivables ($1,487m) far above payables ($1,249m): growth consumes cash, so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE. Set at -15% of the revenue increase in the base (versus ~-40% on the raw NWC/revenue ratio) because the $500m inventory-release programme (gross inventory down from $2,467m to $2,113m over 12 months) offsets most organic NWC growth through the explicit horizon.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2: non-US operating company, cyclical/defensive mix) with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied for (a) USD statements vs GBp quote, (b) leases, (d) excluded associate income with the asset in the bridge, (f) risk charged once. Chosen because Smith & Nephew is a conventional device manufacturer whose value is its unlevered cash flow; nothing in the capital structure (investment-grade net debt 1.8x, no NCI, no deposits, no fair-value assets) argues for another model. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). last_fcf = reported_fcf 852 (OCF 1,285 - capex 433, FY2025) - SBC 43 - interest_income 0 = 809: interest income ($28m) is NOT stripped because the company is a net-debt (not net-cash) issuer and no cash pile is added to EV. Note reported FCF is post-interest-paid ($142m, classified in operating under IFRS); the projections are unlevered, built from EBITDA -> tax -> capex -> working capital, so net debt is deducted once. Revenue is modelled in USD reported terms: FY2026 guidance is ~4% underlying = ~5.2% reported at 31 July 2026 FX; H1 FY2026 reported +4.6%. Integrity Orthopaedics (closed Jan 2026, $225m cash + $165m fair-valued earn-out) is in FY2026 flows (guided $20-25m trading-profit dilutive, neutral 2027, accretive 2028) and its earn-out is deducted in the equity bridge.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in associates (Bioventus stake) and other investments at book
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 balance sheet: associates $126m + investments $25m. Share of associates' results is excluded from the flows, so the asset enters the bridge (adaptations rule d). Book, not fair value -- conservative.
H1 FY2026 acquisition note: $165m discounted value of milestone payments over 3 years (up to $225m nominal). Debt-like, sits in other payables, not in net debt.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr blended with FY2026 guidance (~4% underlying / ~5.2% reported) and the RISE 2026-28 target (6-7%) haircut for the in-year miss
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges >30% from revenue (5.7-6.2%) and EPS CAGRs: equity is flat because the company distributes essentially all attributable profit ($330m dividends + $502m buybacks in FY2025 against $625m profit) and took a $159m inventory provision; it is not a signal of a shrinking business, so revenue/guidance rather than equity CAGR anchors growth. EPS and FCF 3-yr CAGRs are off the FY2022 trough (EPS 25.5c, owner FCF $70m) and are not repeatable.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped, net-debt issuer): FY2020 466, FY2021 428, FY2022 70, FY2023 142, FY2024 566, FY2025 809. 5-yr owner-FCF CAGR 11.7% (from 466) vs reported 11.6% -- SBC is small (~0.7% of revenue) and flat, so the SBC adjustment barely moves the growth rates; the swing is the FY2022-23 inventory build and its reversal. Revenue: FY2020 4,560 -> FY2025 6,164 (6.2% CAGR, flattered by the COVID-depressed FY2020 base); FY2022 5,215 -> FY2025 6,164 (5.7%). Equity: FY2020 5,279 -> FY2025 5,289. EPS: FY2020 51.2c -> FY2025 71.6c (6.9%); FY2022 25.5c -> FY2025 71.6c (41.1%, trough base).

base.growth_note: FY2026 5.0% reported (~4% underlying guided 2026-08-04 after the cut from ~6%, plus FX at 31 July rates; H1 reported +4.6%). FY2027-29 at 5.0-5.5%: the RISE 6-7% organic target haircut ~1.5pp for the in-year miss, US Knees not inflecting until LANDMARK ramps in 2027, China VBP extending to ENT, and the skin-substitute reset; market growth is ~6%, so base is modest share loss in Ortho offset by Sports Med/AWM share gains. Fades to 2.5% by year 10.
base.margin_note: Owner basis (adjusted EBITDA less ~1.5pp recurring restructuring/integration/legal cash, fading to ~1.0pp). FY2026 24.8%: guided trading profit ~$1.3bn on ~$6.47bn revenue = 20.1% trading margin + ~6.2pp D&A ex acquisition amortisation = ~26.3% adjusted, less 1.5pp. Expands ~170bps to 26.5% by year 6 -- below the RISE-implied ~22% trading margin by 2028 (9-10% TP CAGR on 6-7% revenue) because base revenue is lower and operating leverage with it; the $325-375m gross savings programme and the Ortho 300-400bps margin target are partly credited.
base.capex_note: FY2026 7.2% (H1 $190m annualised plus Hull wound factory, ERP and IT upgrades, guided not to repeat in H2); fades to 6.8%, the FY2021-25 average (7.2%) less the completed 8-to-3 Ortho site consolidation. D&A ex-ROU 5.6% leaves ~1.2pp of net investment, consistent with 4-5% growth and continued capitalised software/development.
base.tax_note: Cash tax ramps 16% -> 20%: FY2025 paid $147m (~14% of modelled EBIT) against a guided 19-20% P&L rate on trading results.

bull.narrative_note: RISE delivered: 6-7% organic growth FY2027-29 as LANDMARK Knee, CATALYSTEM Hip, TESSA and REGENETEN/Tendon Seam ramp, Sports Med stays >8%, skin substitutes recover from the 2026 transition year; trading margin reaches ~22-23% by 2028 and Ortho >20% by 2030 (adjusted EBITDA ~29.5-30%, less ~1.0pp residual restructuring = 28.5%). Inventory release ($500m capital employed) funds growth so WC drag is only -10%. Cevian-driven simplification (e.g. a Wound separation) is a free option on top, not modelled.

bear.narrative_note: Sub-scale Ortho keeps losing share to Stryker/Zimmer/DePuy (US Knees never inflect, LANDMARK lands late and small), skin substitutes do not recover beyond 2026, China VBP spreads, and restructuring never ends so the FY2026 cost-driven margin step-up (tariff refunds, $200m savings) is the peak: owner margin slips back to 24%. Growth 2-3%, below market. Inventory programme stalls, so NWC growth drags at -25%. Terminal growth 2.0% and a 15x cap for a structurally slower, serial-restructuring business. No solvency axis: 1.8x leverage and $4.7bn committed facilities.

scenario_narratives.base: Smith & Nephew delivers roughly two-thirds of RISE. FY2026 lands at the cut guidance (~4% underlying, ~$1.3bn trading profit, ~$800m FCF) with the step-up in trading profit driven by the $200m efficiency programme and tariff refunds rather than revenue. FY2027-29 revenue grows 5-5.5% as LANDMARK Knee and CATALYSTEM Hip stop the US Ortho bleed without recapturing share, Sports Medicine & ENT keeps compounding above market, and Advanced Wound Management grows mid-single-digit once the skin-substitute reimbursement reset annualises. Owner EBITDA margin expands ~170bps over six years to 26.5% (trading margin low-21s%), short of the 2028 target; restructuring cash keeps running at ~1-1.5% of revenue because it always has. Capex settles at 6.8% after the Hull factory and ERP, working capital drag is muted by the $500m inventory release, cash tax normalises to 20%. The second $500m buyback completes and the count is held flat thereafter.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 12-Point Plan's cash and margin delivery (FCF $56m -> $840m in three years, trading margin +240bps) repeats under RISE: 6-7% organic growth in 2027-29 from the new-product cadence (LANDMARK, CATALYSTEM, TESSA, Tendon Seam, ALLEVYN COMPLETE CARE), continued ASC and Emerging Markets share gains, and a skin-substitute recovery. Trading margin reaches 22-23% by 2028 and Ortho crosses 20% by 2030, taking owner EBITDA margin to 28.5%. Leverage falls below 1.5x, funding bolt-ons and further buybacks. Cevian's ~11.9% stake pushes a portfolio simplification that re-rates the group toward large-cap medtech multiples; that re-rating is upside to, not inside, the 18x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2026 guidance cut was the tell: US Orthopaedics, 40% of revenue and sub-scale at ~7% share, keeps underperforming a ~6% market, LANDMARK arrives late into a cementless market that Stryker and Zimmer already own, China VBP reaches ENT, and the CMS skin-substitute reset proves permanent rather than transitional. Revenue grows 2-3%, trading profit growth is sustained only by cost-cutting that eventually runs out, and a third 'rationalisation' programme follows the second, so the owner margin drifts back to 24%. Inventory release stalls and working capital consumes cash again. Terminal growth 2.0% with a 15x cap. Not a solvency case (investment grade, 1.8x), but a value-trap case: the stock stays cheap because the cash flow never compounds.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: management cut FY2026 revenue guidance from ~6% to ~4% within the year, US Ortho has underperformed for several years with no inflection until 2027, and the skin-substitute reset is a live regulatory loss, so a multi-year value-trap path is a genuine quarter-probability outcome. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs LANDMARK, Ortho margin expansion, a skin-substitute recovery and China VBP navigation to go right together, though the 12-Point Plan's delivered cash record and Cevian's stake keep it a real scenario. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF in USD, converted to pence at the spot GBP/USD rate. The company's own adjusted EBITDA and trading profit are NOT taken at face value: recurring restructuring, integration and legal cash (~$130m/yr, $150m+ in 2024) is charged inside the owner margin because this company has restructured every year for a decade. SBC is small and fully expensed; the count is held flat. Leases are an operating cost, so net debt excludes lease liabilities. Interest income is left in because the company is a net-debt issuer. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights, at a single 8.0% USD WACC. The terminal value is capped at 18x year-10 owner FCF (15x in the bear), roughly the market's mature-medtech multiple and well below large-cap peers, so no re-rating is assumed. The Cevian break-up option and any fair-value uplift on the Bioventus stake are deliberately left out of the numbers.
key_risks_to_valuation: FX: the GBp value moves one-for-one with GBP/USD; the fx_rate is dated 2026-10-09 and is not refreshed by price refreshes.
Margin basis: if the 2026 restructuring wave really is the last, the owner margin is ~1pp too low and value ~8-10% too low; if a third wave follows, the bear is the base.
US Orthopaedics share: every 1pp of sustained growth across the horizon is worth roughly 8-10% of value; LANDMARK's 2027 ramp is the single biggest swing factor.
Working-capital release: the $500m inventory programme is assumed to largely offset NWC growth; if it stalls the base loses ~$50m/yr of FCF.
Terminal cap: at 8% WACC and 2.5% growth Gordon implies ~18.6x, so the 18x cap binds in base and bull; value is terminal-heavy (>55%) as for any mature compounder.
Contingent liabilities not in the bridge: legacy earn-outs (CartiHeal) and product-liability exposure are unquantified.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for SN.L (GBp) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 980.4-1426.59p. GBPUSD=X and the SNN ADR used for the fx_note parity check.
data_sources.financials: SN.L_Metrics.csv (FY2018-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2019-H1 FY2026 interim, USD millions) derived from the FY2019-FY2025 Annual Reports (20-F form) and the H1 FY2026 results release; balance-sheet anchors from the H1 FY2026 condensed statements and Note 6 (net debt); adjusted EBITDA and trading-profit reconciliations from the FY2025 Annual Report non-IFRS section.

sanity_check_note.status: passes on the real multiples; the script's printed multiples are the documented dual-currency fx-direction bug
sanity_check_note.detail: scripts/sanity_check.py multiplies the historical GBp prices by fx_rate (75.57) and leaves the implied GBp IV unconverted against USD per-share metrics, so it prints implied P/B 215x vs a 16,669x historical average and passes by accident (same false pass recorded in memory for AAF.L, HSBA.L, WISE.L). Hand-computed on a consistent USD basis at the base-case IV ($17.24/share, EV $17,475m): P/B 2.8x on $6.24 BVPS (equity $5,289m / 848m), EV/adjusted EBITDA 10.9x on $1,607m (13.2x on SBC-adjusted statutory EBITDA $1,324m), P/S 2.4x; at the current price EV/adjusted EBITDA is ~8.9x. Smith & Nephew's FY2018-25 EV/EBITDA range is roughly 12-18x, so the implied multiples sit at or below history and no fix pass (mid-cycle FCF / WACC premium / growth cap / exit-multiple cap) is warranted.
